result.stdout:
Description:
  Veritas — RDF / SPARQL / SHACL command-line, MCP server (-mcp), and SPARQL HTTP endpoint.

Usage:
  veritas [command] [options]

Options:
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information
  --version       Show version information

Commands:
  query <query-file>  Run a SPARQL SELECT/ASK query over RDF data files.
  serve               Run a SPARQL 1.1 Protocol HTTP endpoint over RDF data files, optionally hosting the Studio UI (--ui).
  analytics           Run a graph-analytics algorithm (degree, triangles, clustering, PageRank, components, cliques) over RDF data files.
  replicate           Run a store-backed replica: serve replication on loopback, reconcile with a peer (remove-aware by default), self-heal over the wire, and optionally coordinate identity and lineage on a consensus metadata plane.

  Run a SPARQL SELECT/ASK query over RDF data files.

  veritas query <query-file> [options]

Arguments:
  <query-file>  Path to a file containing the SPARQL query.

Description:
  Run a SPARQL 1.1 Protocol HTTP endpoint over RDF data files, optionally hosting the Studio UI (--ui).

Usage:
  veritas serve [options]

Options:
  -d, --data <data>            RDF data file (.ttl/.nt/.trig/.nq) to serve; repeat for several.
  -p, --port <port>            Loopback port to listen on (default 3030).
  --ui                         Also serve the in-browser Studio UI (from --ui-dir) at the root and open a browser; its tab queries this engine.
  --ui-dir <ui-dir>            Directory of the built Studio web app (its 'dist') to serve with --ui; defaults to a 'ui' directory beside the executable.
  --no-open                    With --ui, do not open a browser automatically.
  --cors-origin <cors-origin>  Origin allowed cross-origin (CORS) access to the endpoints, e.g. a remotely hosted Studio page; repeat for several, or pass * to allow any origin. Absent, no cross-origin access is granted.
  -?, -h, --help               Show help and usage information

Description:
  Run a graph-analytics algorithm (degree, triangles, clustering, PageRank, components, cliques) over RDF data files.

Usage:
  veritas analytics [options]

Options:
  -a, --algo <algo>      Graph-analytics algorithm name (run with --list to see them).
  -d, --data <data>      RDF data file (.ttl/.nt/.trig/.nq/.rdf/.owl) forming the graph; repeat for several.
  --param <param>        Algorithm parameter as name=value (for example size=4, connectivity=mutual, damping=0.85); repeat.
  -f, --format <format>  Result format: csv (default) or tsv.
  --list                 List the available graph-analytics algorithms.
  -?, -h, --help         Show help and usage information

Description:
  Run a store-backed replica: serve replication on loopback, reconcile with a peer (remove-aware by default), self-heal over the wire, and optionally coordinate identity and lineage on a consensus metadata plane.

Usage:
  veritas replicate [options]

Options:
  --store <store> (REQUIRED)                 Store directory the replica opens (created if missing).
  -d, --data <data>                          RDF data file seeding an EMPTY store as the lineage seed; repeat for several.
  --listen <listen>                          Loopback TCP port serving replication to peers; 0 picks an ephemeral port, printed as 'listening <port>'.
  --peer <peer>                              Peer replication endpoint as host:port; also bindable later with the 'peer' verb.
  --reconcile-interval <reconcile-interval>  Seconds between automatic reconcile pulls from the peer; absent pulls only on the 'reconcile' verb.
  --self-heal                                Run the background storage self-heal loop, with both peer-repair seams over the bound peer.
  --heal-interval <heal-interval>            Seconds between self-heal rounds (a fixed cadence, no jitter); absent uses the reliability-model cadence.
  --identity-dir <identity-dir>              Directory the HOST's replica identity is persisted in (minted on first use); absent uses the per-user configuration location. Distinct replicas on one machine each need their own directory.
  --baseline                                 Perform the explicit causality baseline step on a resumed store that is not already remove-aware; the outcome is reported by name on the identity line.
  --metadata-founder <metadata-founder>      Founding member of the consensus metadata chain as <64hex axis>:<32hex store>, which is what the 'axis ... store ...' startup line prints; repeat for every founder.
